summary: Cleared W. H. Teepe, a tabulator on the Post Office Department's mail-weighing work, for a permanent clerical job in the Department without the usual civil-service rules.
Let Robert L. Slagle, an assistant messenger in the Post Office Department, move up to a permanent clerical position there without the usual civil-service rules.
Allowed James H. Adams, who served in the Treasury Department's classified service from 1892 to 1904, to be reinstated without regard to the civil-service rules.
Permitted Gilman B. Howe to be appointed a clerk in the Bureau of the Census without meeting the civil-service rules.
Abolished the Watertown land district in South Dakota, sending its lands, business and records to the Aberdeen land district.
Reserved certain described lands at Haines, Alaska, for educational purposes.
Allowed John E. Kidwell, an accountant (pay clerk) in the Isthmian Canal service, to transfer to a classified clerical position in the United States.
Let Frank O'Neill return as a stock examiner in the Department of Agriculture, waiving the civil-service rule's one-year limit on reinstatement.
Set apart public lands at Cape Fanshaw, Alaska, where Frederick Sound meets Fanshaw Bay, as a military reservation to protect and maintain a cable station.
Created the Toiyabe Forest Reserve in Nevada, setting aside public lands partly covered with timber and reserving them from settlement.
Enlarged the Wenaha Forest Reserve, which straddles Oregon and Washington, by adding timbered lands on the Oregon side.
Added timbered lands in Oregon to the Siskiyou Forest Reserve, created just months earlier in October 1906.
Stretched the Big Hole Forest Reserve of Montana across the state line, adding timbered lands in Idaho.
Enlarged the Uncompahgre Forest Reserve in Colorado with additional lands partly covered with timber.
Redrew the Big Belt Forest Reserve in Montana, adding timbered lands and cutting out others, which were restored and opened to settlement.
Combined Oregon's Wallowa and Chesnimnus forest reserves, plus added lands, into one new reserve: the Imnaha Forest Reserve.
Changed the boundaries of the Park Range Forest Reserve in Colorado, adding timbered lands and excluding others, which were opened to settlement.
Enlarged the Holy Cross Forest Reserve in Colorado with additional lands partly covered with timber.
Established the Bear Lodge Forest Reserve in Wyoming, setting apart timbered public lands and reserving them from settlement.
Established the Colville Forest Reserve in Washington on timbered public lands, with margin notes addressing allotments to Indians.
Created the Las Animas Forest Reserve on timbered public lands spanning Colorado and the Territory of New Mexico.
Rewrote ration rules at the Army and Navy General Hospital in Hot Springs, Arkansas, paying 30 cents per ration for soldiers, nurses, sailors and Marines instead of issuing food in kind.
Established the Little Rockies Forest Reserve in Montana, setting apart public lands partly covered with timber.
Redrew the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, adding timbered lands in Wyoming, Montana and Idaho and excluding others, which were opened to settlement.
Set apart the Port Neuf Forest Reserve in Idaho on public lands partly covered with timber.
Set apart the Palouse Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving timbered public lands from settlement.
Adjusted the Weiser Forest Reserve in Idaho again, adding timbered lands and excluding others, which were reopened to settlement.
Set apart the Cabinet Forest Reserve on timbered public lands in Montana and Idaho.
Enlarged the Mt. Rainier Forest Reserve in Washington with more timbered land and, per the margin notes, changed its name to the Rainier Forest Reserve.
Modified the Washington Forest Reserve, excluding some lands and adding new timbered tracts in Washington; excluded lands were opened to settlement.
Further enlarged the Ashland Forest Reserve in Oregon with additional lands partly covered with timber.
Set apart the Coquille Forest Reserve in Oregon on public lands partly covered with timber.
Added more timbered Oregon land to the Cascade Forest Reserve, first created in 1893 as the Cascade Range Forest Reserve.
Set apart the Umpqua Forest Reserve in Oregon, reserving timbered public lands from settlement.
Folded Oregon's Maury Mountain Forest Reserve into the Blue Mountains Forest Reserve and enlarged the combined reserve with additional lands.
Further enlarged the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve with timbered lands in Colorado and Wyoming.
Added more timbered Montana land to the Lewis and Clark Forest Reserve, established in 1897.
Set apart the Otter Forest Reserve in Montana on public lands partly covered with timber.
Further enlarged the Olympic Forest Reserve in Washington with additional lands partly covered with timber.
Enlarged the Montezuma Forest Reserve in Colorado with additional timbered lands.
Enlarged the San Juan Forest Reserve in Colorado, created in 1905, with more lands partly covered with timber.
Further enlarged the Priest River Forest Reserve with timbered lands in Idaho and Washington.
Set apart the Tillamook Forest Reserve in Oregon on public lands partly covered with timber.
Reserved the southern tip of the Cape Spencer headland at the entrance to Cross Sound, Alaska, with nearby islands and land around Dick's Arm, for lighthouse purposes.
Directed that coal-land withdrawals included within forest reserves by proclamation are not to be excluded from the operation of those proclamations.
Allowed Lillie L. Wright, a former Patent Office clerk, to be reinstated no matter how long she had been out of the service.
Named John F. Stevens chairman of the Isthmian Canal Commission and George W. Goethals a member.
Allowed George W. Pitts to be appointed a Treasury Department clerk without meeting the civil-service rules.
Barred subordinates in the Department of Justice from publishing legal opinions without the Attorney General's approval.
Let James G. Massey be appointed to a clerical position in the Department of the Interior without reference to civil-service rules.
Allowed John C. Eversman, Sr., a special examiner in the Pension Office, to be appointed or transferred to a competitive position there.
Let P. J. Hughes, who left the Isthmian Canal service because of ill health, be reinstated and transferred as a clerk to the War Department.
Allowed C. F. House to be hired as a $1,000-a-year clerk at the Great Lakes Naval Training Station in North Chicago, Illinois, without civil-service rules.
Proclaimed Chaco Canyon National Monument in New Mexico, protecting its prehistoric pueblo ruins and burial grounds, described as being of extraordinary interest for their number, size and relics.
Designated F. C. Ainsworth and J. Franklin Bell to serve as Acting Secretary of War.
Issued regulations for executing and recording deeds in the Canal Zone, effective April 15, 1907.
Split the Canal Zone into four administrative districts (Ancon, Emperador, Gorgona and Cristobal), each with a tax collector taking over municipal treasury and assessment duties.
Amended the Canal Zone's Penal Code, revising punishments for assault, battery, failure to support a wife or child, grand larceny and embezzlement of public funds.
Allowed ministers in regular standing, judges of courts of record and municipal or district judges to perform marriages in the Canal Zone.
Changed civil-service Rule II so post offices newly given free delivery come under the rules, but staff appointed within 60 days of the change aren't classified without Commission consent.

Barred Japanese and Korean laborers holding passports to Mexico, Canada or Hawaii from entering the continental United States from those places, and told the Secretary of Commerce and Labor to enforce it.
Allowed R. H. Mitchell to be appointed a watchman in the Department of the Interior without examination.
Let Dr. A. Brown join the Department of Agriculture without examination, citing his special ability for work under the pure-food and drugs law.
Moved parts of the Great Falls land district in Montana into the Glasgow land district.
Revoked the Portales National Forest in New Mexico, no longer needed for experimental forest purposes, and returned its lands to the public domain, open to settlement.
Appointed Maj. William L. Sibert, Maj. David Du B. Gaillard and Civil Engineer Harry H. Rousseau to the Isthmian Canal Commission at $14,000 a year, replacing three members who resigned.
Allowed Charles P. Galpin, a Pension Office messenger, to be appointed to a clerical position there without examination.
Amended the March 4 order to give Isthmian Canal Commissioner George W. Goethals a furnished house on the Isthmus and expenses for official travel away from it.
Let Frederick M. Kerby be appointed to a clerical position in the Department of the Interior without reference to civil-service rules.
Permitted Harlan Updegraff to be appointed Alaskan assistant in the Bureau of Education without reference to civil-service rules.
Put a Code of Civil Procedure into effect for the Canal Zone.
Allowed Mahlon Pursel to be reinstated as a clerk in the War Department's Adjutant-General's Office despite the civil-service time limit on reinstatement.
Allowed F. T. Quinlan to be reinstated as an inspector of furs in the quartermaster's department at Philadelphia.
Let W. P. Armstrong, a law clerk with the Isthmian Canal Commission, transfer to another competitive position paying up to $2,500 a year, waiving transfer-rule limits.
Allowed Theresa S. Aubright to be appointed to a clerical position in the classified civil service without examination.
Called the general election of delegates to the Philippine Assembly, the popular assembly that would share legislative power with the Philippine Commission under the 1902 act of Congress.
Allowed one clerk or examiner to be appointed as private secretary to the Commissioner of the General Land Office without reference to civil-service rules.
Allowed James Bronson Reynolds to be appointed a Chinese inspector in the Immigration Service without civil-service examination.
Enlarged the Grande Island military reservation off Luzon in the Philippines to take in all rocks, shoals and islands within one mile of the island's low-water line.
Made Lt. Col. George W. Goethals chairman of the Isthmian Canal Commission, succeeding John F. Stevens, who resigned.
Appointed Joseph C. S. Blackburn to the Isthmian Canal Commission at $14,000 a year, with a furnished house on the Isthmus and travel expenses.
Let Jake T. Patrick, a storekeeper-gauger in Kentucky's eighth internal-revenue district, transfer to a competitive position in that district.
Made four hours a full Saturday's work in July, August and September for civilian mechanics, laborers and other employees at War Department arsenals, depots and Army headquarters offices.
Enlarged the Big Burros National Forest in the Territory of New Mexico with additional lands partly covered with timber.
Rewrote diplomatic and consular rules on citizenship and passports, covering children of citizens born abroad, wives of citizens, and American women who marry foreigners.
Updated consular regulations so consulates keep, and publicize, a register of American citizens living in their districts.
Corrected the boundaries of the Camp Downes military reservation at Ormoc, Leyte, in the Philippines after a survey found the original metes and bounds were wrong.
Excused Spanish War veterans in the District of Columbia from duty on April 12 so they could attend the unveiling of the Rough Riders Monument at Arlington.
Allowed John H. McTeer, a skilled laborer in the Treasury Department, to be promoted to clerk after passing the exam before completing two years in a subclerical grade.
Set apart the Toquima National Forest in Nevada on public lands partly covered with timber, "for the use and benefit of the people."
Enlarged the Gallinas National Forest in the Territory of New Mexico with additional timbered lands.
Set apart the Monitor National Forest in Nevada, reserving timbered public lands from settlement or entry.

Rewrote the civil-service transfer rule: transfers require six months' classified service, and moves between Washington departments or independent offices require three years, which the Commission may waive.
Abolished the Gunnison land district in Colorado and transferred its business to the Montrose land district.
Created the Guadalupe National Forest in the Territory of New Mexico on public lands partly covered with timber.
